# Nightly backup of the orders database
*Automated nightly dump, retention and restore check for orders data*

This plan sets up a nightly backup of the orders database so we can recover from data loss or a bad deploy. Please review the schedule, retention and where backups are stored before it goes live.

## What gets backed up and when
- A full logical dump of the orders database runs every night at 02:00 UTC, when order traffic is lowest.
- The dump is compressed and named with its date and time, so each night's backup is distinct.
- Connection details come from environment variables, never from the script itself.

## Where backups live and how long we keep them
- Each dump is written to a local backup directory, then copied to off-site object storage.
- Local copies are kept for 7 days; off-site copies for 30 days.
- Older backups are pruned automatically after each successful run.

## How we'll know it works
- The job exits with an error and logs it if the dump, compression or upload fails, so the scheduler can alert.
- Each dump is checked for integrity right after it is written.
- Once a month, someone restores the latest backup into a scratch database and checks that recent orders are present.

## Question: Where should off-site copies go?
- A. Our existing cloud object storage bucket, in a separate backup bucket (recommended)
- B. Local disk only for now, off-site later
- C. A second database server in another region

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Nightly backup of the orders database.
#
# Schedule (cron, 02:00 UTC):
#   0 2 * * * /path/to/scripts/backup.sh >> /var/log/orders-backup.log 2>&1
#
# Configuration (environment variables):
#   PGHOST, PGPORT, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD  standard Postgres connection settings
#   ORDERS_DB              database name (default: orders)
#   BACKUP_DIR             local backup directory (default: /var/backups/orders)
#   LOCAL_RETENTION_DAYS   days to keep local copies (default: 7)
#   BACKUP_S3_URI          optional off-site target, e.g. s3://orders-backups/nightly
#                          (off-site retention of 30 days is set as a bucket lifecycle rule)

set -euo pipefail

ORDERS_DB="${ORDERS_DB:-orders}"
BACKUP_DIR="${BACKUP_DIR:-/var/backups/orders}"
LOCAL_RETENTION_DAYS="${LOCAL_RETENTION_DAYS:-7}"
BACKUP_S3_URI="${BACKUP_S3_URI:-}"

log() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$*"; }
fail() { log "ERROR: $*"; exit 1; }

for cmd in pg_dump pg_restore; do
  command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null || fail "$cmd not found"
done
if [[ -n "$BACKUP_S3_URI" ]]; then
  command -v aws >/dev/null || fail "aws CLI not found but BACKUP_S3_URI is set"
fi

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"
timestamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
final="$BACKUP_DIR/${ORDERS_DB}-${timestamp}.dump"
tmp="$final.partial"
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

log "Starting backup of $ORDERS_DB to $final"
# Custom format is compressed and restorable with pg_restore.
pg_dump --format=custom --compress=9 --no-owner --file="$tmp" "$ORDERS_DB" \
  || fail "pg_dump failed"

# Integrity check: pg_restore must be able to read the archive's table of contents.
pg_restore --list "$tmp" >/dev/null || fail "integrity check failed for $tmp"
[[ -s "$tmp" ]] || fail "dump is empty"

mv "$tmp" "$final"
log "Dump written ($(du -h "$final" | cut -f1))"

if [[ -n "$BACKUP_S3_URI" ]]; then
  aws s3 cp --only-show-errors "$final" "${BACKUP_S3_URI%/}/$(basename "$final")" \
    || fail "off-site upload failed"
  log "Uploaded to $BACKUP_S3_URI"
fi

# Prune local copies only after a successful run.
find "$BACKUP_DIR" -name "${ORDERS_DB}-*.dump" -type f -mtime +"$LOCAL_RETENTION_DAYS" -print -delete \
  | while read -r f; do log "Pruned $f"; done

log "Backup complete"
